arxiv-2207-06254.title: Towards Knowledge-based Mining of Mental Disorder Patterns from Textual Data
arxiv-2207-06254.creator: Maryam Shahabikargar*
arxiv-2207-06254.description: Abstract abstract Mental health disorders may cause severe consequences on all the countries’ economies and health. For example, the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, such as isolation and travel ban, can make us feel depressed. Identifying early signs of mental health disorders is vital. For example, depression may increase an individual’s risk of suicide.

arxiv-2209-01037.title: Discordant edges for the voter model on regular random graphs
arxiv-2209-01037.creator: Luca Avena, Rangel Baldasso, Rajat Subhra Hazra, Frank den Hollander, Matteo Quattropani
arxiv-2209-01037.description: Abstract . We consider the two-opinion voter model on a regular random graph with n n vertices and degree d ≥ 3 d\geq 3 . It is known that consensus is reached on time scale n n and that on this time scale the volume of the set of vertices with one opinion evolves as a Fisher-Wright diffusion.

arxiv-2307-14739.title: AUDIO INPUTS FOR ACTIVE SPEAKER DETECTION AND LOCALIZATION VIA MICROPHONE ARRAY
arxiv-2307-14739.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . This study considers the problem of detecting and locating an active talker’s horizontal position from multichannel audio captured by a microphone array. We refer to this as active speaker detection and localization (ASDL). Our goal was to investigate the performance of spatial acoustic features extracted from the multichannel audio as the input of a convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN), in relation to the number of channels employed and additive noise.

arxiv-2506-04698.title: NEAT and HyperNEAT based Design for Soft Actuator Controllers
arxiv-2506-04698.creator: Hugo Alcaraz-Herrera, Michail-Antisthenis Tsompanas, Igor Balaz, Andrew Adamatzky
arxiv-2506-04698.description: Abstract Since soft robotics are composed of compliant materials, they perform better than conventional rigid robotics in specific fields, such as medical applications. However, the field of soft robotics is fairly new, and the design process of their morphology and their controller strategies has not yet been thoroughly studied.

arxiv-2508-09871.title: Inference of germinal center evolutionary dynamics via simulation-based deep learning
arxiv-2508-09871.creator: Duncan K Ralph
arxiv-2508-09871.description: Abstract Abstract B cells and the antibodies they produce are vital to health and survival, motivating research on the details of the mutational and evolutionary processes in the germinal centers (GCs) from which mature B cells arise. It is known that B cells with higher affinity for their cognate antigen (Ag) will, on average, tend to have more offspring.

arxiv-2601-04913.title: Bayesian Additive Regression Tree Copula Processes for Scalable Distributional Prediction
arxiv-2601-04913.creator: Jan Martin Wenkel, Michael Stanley Smith, Nadja Klein
arxiv-2601-04913.description: Abstract We show how to construct the implied copula process of response values from a Bayesian additive regression tree (BART) model with prior on the leaf node variances. This copula process, defined on the covariate space, can be paired with any marginal distribution for the dependent variable to construct a flexible distributional BART model.

europmc-pmc1874167.description: Steroidal estrogens, originating principally from human excretion, are likely to play a major role in causing widespread endocrine disruption in wild populations of the roach (Rutilus rutilus), a common cyprinid fish, in rivers contaminated by treated sewage effluents. pmc-11428584.title: Effects and Mechanisms of Lutein on Aging and Age-Related Diseases
pmc-11428584.creator: Jialu Ye, Jin Cheng, Ruogu Xiong, Haoqi Chen, Siyu Huang, Huabin Li, Jinzhu Pang, Xuguang Zhang, Huilian Zhu
pmc-11428584.description: Aging and age-related diseases are serious public health issues that are receiving growing attention from researchers. Lutein has a critical function in the prevention and management of these issues. Possible mechanisms mainly include suppressing inflammation and oxidative stress, regulating cell activity, and modulating the levels of toxic substances.

pmc-11713132.title: Exploring Alzheimer’s disease progression through the lens of genetics and sleep disturbances
pmc-11713132.creator: Leticia Fernandez‐Moguel, Ifrah Gobdon, Azizi A Seixas, Arzu Çöltekin, David Dedic, Alberto R Ramos
pmc-11713132.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundT/S ratio represents the average telomere length per genome, and has been previously linked to Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) and biological sex [1], but there is a gap in our understanding of its interactions with sleep patterns.

pmc-11805079.title: Effect of Bleaching on Surface Roughness of White Spot Lesions Treated with Different Modalities of Resin Infiltration: An Vitro Study
pmc-11805079.creator: Aidel Abdullah Alshahrani, Afra Elrashid
pmc-11805079.description: Background:This experimental study evaluated the effect of resin infiltrant (RI) application modalities and bleaching on surface roughness (SR) of the RI white spot lesions (WSLs).Methods:Ninety-six extracted sound premolar teeth were selected, and their coronal part was embedded in a self-cure acrylic resin block.

pmc-12608925.title: Reclassifying Menopausal Breast Cancer and Assessing Non-Genetic Risk Factors in Ghanaian Women: Insights from a Cohort Study
pmc-12608925.creator: Claudia Adzo Anyigba, Victor Ayinbora Azusiyine, Courage Siame, Aniefiok John Udoakang, Emmanuel Lante Lamptey, Christiana Dufie Asamoah, Helena Frempong, Gordon Akanzuwine Awandare, Josephine Nsaful, Joe Nat Clegg-Lamptey, Florence Dedey, Lawrence Edusei, Ralph Armah, Alfred Twumasi, Ronald J Weige
pmc-12608925.description: Simple SummaryBreast cancer is a multifactorial disease, with racial variations often observed in its presentation. These variations are influenced by population-specific risk factors and reproductive health characteristics. Menopausal age is used as a basis for classifying breast cancer, with most studies using 50 years as a proxy for the global menopausal age.

pmc-12621641.title: Assembly strategy for thieno[3,2-b]thiophenes via a disulfide intermediate derived from 3-nitrothiophene-2,5-dicarboxylate
pmc-12621641.creator: Roman A Irgashev
pmc-12621641.description: A versatile synthetic route to thieno[3,2-b]thiophenes was elaborated from dimethyl 3-nitrothiophene-2,5-dicarboxylate. Nucleophilic substitution of the nitro group with sulfur nucleophiles, including thioacetate or disulfide anions as well as thioacetamide, yielded bis(thiophen-3-yl)disulfide and sulfide derivatives. The disulfide served as a suitable precursor for the preparation of 3-alkylthio-substituted thiophene-2,5-dicarboxylates by its one-pot reduction–alkylation using NaBH4 in DMF followed by an alkylating agent.

pmc-12623153.title: CXCL10 Involvement in Vestibular Migraine via the PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathway
pmc-12623153.creator: Mao‐mei Song, Ting‐yan Chen, Shi‐na Song, Ying‐jie Gao, Chang‐xin Li, Sui‐yi Xu
pmc-12623153.description: AimsC‐X‐C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10) is a member of the CXC chemokine family, known as a classical pain‐related chemokine. While CXCL10 is implicated in neuropathic pain, its role in vestibular migraine (VM) remains unclear.MethodsSerum CXCL10 levels correlated with dizziness and headache severity in VM patients.

pmc-12717342.title: Chainmail catalysis for advanced water treatment: overcoming the stability–reactivity tradeoff in Fenton-like oxidation of micropollutants
pmc-12717342.creator: Quang Viet Ly, Lele Cui, Yuri Park, Long D. Nghiem, Hanh Tien Nguyen, Van-Duong Dao, Soryong Chae, Yuhoon Hwang
pmc-12717342.description: Recent developments in chainmail catalysis present a promising solution to the longstanding challenge of catalytic deactivation in traditional advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) for water reuse. This strategy involves encapsulating nanocatalysts within protective carbon shells, which significantly improves their stability and enhances the degradation kinetics of micropollutants.

pmc-12787912.title: Systematic Control of Epoxidation in Low-cis Hydroxyl-Terminated Polybutadiene (HTPB) and Its Impact on Polyurethane Properties
pmc-12787912.creator: Sungyoung Yoon, Jongbok Lee
pmc-12787912.description: Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) is widely used in polyurethane binders, adhesives, and elastomers, but its low polarity and unsaturated backbone limit adhesion and long-term stability. Epoxidation presents a promising approach to addressing these limitations. However, most prior studies have focused on high-cis polybutadiene (PB), and systematic tuning of epoxidation in industrial low-cis HTPB has not been thoroughly examined.

pmc-13066881.title: Left ventricular parameters and mass indexing methods in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging in prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events and mortality
pmc-13066881.creator: Patrycja S Matusik, Jarosław D Jarczewski, Mateusz Nawrocki, Tomasz Górecki, Aleksandra Jarczewska, Janina Schwarz, Katarzyna Mikrut, Agnieszka Pac, Tadeusz J Popiela, Paweł T Matusik
pmc-13066881.description: BackgroundIncreased left ventricular mass (LVM) is a predictor of adverse outcomes. We investigated which cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging parameters and LVM indexing methods are associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) and mortality.MethodsIn this exploratory analysis, we included patients with known cardiovascular diseases who underwent CMR.

pmc-13376856.title: Risk Factors for Cardiovascular Disease: Epidemiology, Screening, Prevention, and Therapeutic Interventions
pmc-13376856.creator: Mowei Kong, Zaiyong Zheng, Min Huang, Shengyu Huang, Xingwei Zhao, Yang Yu, Chunxiang Zhang
pmc-13376856.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the burden is particularly severe in low‐income and middle‐income countries. Although traditional risk factors such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, and smoking have been well established, new research evidence indicates that inflammation, environmental exposure, psychological and social stress, gut microbiota, and genetic susceptibility play a crucial role in shaping the risk profile of CVDs.

pmc-13543797.title: Infection-triggered encephalopathy syndromes: a meta-analysis of clinical characteristics and outcomes in 1946 cases
pmc-13543797.creator: Michael Eyre, Velda X. Han, Terrence Thomas, Hiroshi Sakuma, Shekeeb S. Mohammad, Hannah F. Jones, Takayuki Mori, Go Kawano, Vanessa W. Lee, Stephen Malone, Carly Debinski, Hiroya Nishida, Margherita Nosadini, Ming Lim, Russell C. Dale
pmc-13543797.description: SummaryBackgroundInfection-triggered encephalopathy syndromes (ITES) are acute, para-infectious disorders that can cause disability or death. Recognition is increasingly important in viral pandemics, but clinical features and outcomes remain poorly understood.MethodsPubMed search (inception to 6 March 2024) identified studies with published individual patient data (raw data were not collected from authors).

pmc-13680340.title: Family screening for genetic cardiomyopathies in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents: a joint clinical and genetic approach
pmc-13680340.creator: Mark Abela, Jessica Debattista, Jeanesse Scerri, Tiziana Felice, Victor Grech, Christian Scerri
pmc-13680340.description: Adolescents may present with abnormal ECG findings despite having no structural or electrical evidence of cardiomyopathy. The value of extending family screening to this subgroup remains uncertain. To evaluate the impact of family screening in ECG-positive phenotype-negative adolescents, and determine whether a joint clinical-genetic approach improves the diagnostic yield.

pmc-13722875.title: OVATE family protein 6 interacts with CONSTANS-LIKE 3 to regulate bolting by transcriptional control of FLOWERING LOCUS T/TERMINAL FLOWER 1 family genes in lettuce
pmc-13722875.creator: Guanghui An, Ruoqing Liu, Xinhui Zhao, Yueji Wang, Chenxi Li, Lei Zhu, Luming Yang, Peinan Sun, Yong Wang
pmc-13722875.description: As one of the most globally cultivated vegetables, lettuce’s commercial yield is severely compromised by premature bolting, an undesirable agronomic trait that diminishes crop quality and market value. In this study, we genetically cloned the OVATE family protein 6 (LsOFP6) controlling bolting time in lettuce. LsOFP6 had a nonsense mutation in the late bolting parent.
